programme: STAT1, IRF1 and IRF2 form the canonical interferon-gamma-driven transcriptional module that induces antigen presentation (TAP1/TAP2, PSMB9, CIITA, HLA-E) and PD-L1; TBX21 marks the Th1/CD8 cytotoxic effector programme that supplies the IFN-gamma driving that module; IKZF1 is the lymphoid master regulator required for the T- and B-cell compartments that execute it; AIRE and FOXN1 govern thymic central tolerance, the counterweight that determines whether disrupting this axis with checkpoint blockade produces tumour control or autoimmune toxicity.
role_in_a: In lung cancer this axis sets the tumour's interferon-inflamed phenotype: STAT1/IRF1/IRF2 downstream of IFN-gamma drive MHC-I/II antigen presentation and PD-L1 induction in NSCLC cells, IKZF1 marks lymphoid infiltration and is used as a methylation biomarker in adenocarcinoma, TBX21 indexes the Th1/CD8 infiltrate that radiotherapy and dendritic-cell-directed therapies try to expand, and FOXN1 is a reported prognostic marker in squamous NSCLC.
role_in_b: In melanoma the same core (STAT1, IRF2) sets IFN-gamma-driven PD-L1 expression and ferroptosis susceptibility, and IRF1 acts through SOX10-dependent and TRIM21-linked circuits to shape metastasis and anti-tumour immunity; TBX21 and IKZF1 mark the cytotoxic/lymphoid state that predicts anti-PD-1 survival; AIRE, and to a lesser extent FOXN1 (via thymic/keratinocyte biology), are implicated in the central-tolerance breakdown that produces immune-related adverse events when melanoma patients are put on checkpoint inhibitors.
shared_axis: Lung cancer and melanoma are the two paradigm 'immunogenic' solid tumours whose response to checkpoint blockade is governed by the same tumour-intrinsic IFN-gamma/JAK-STAT antigen-presentation circuit and the same cytotoxic T-cell/thymic-tolerance circuitry, so a factor set built from STAT1, IRF1, IRF2, TBX21, IKZF1, AIRE and FOXN1 recurring across independently-stratified patient groups of both diseases is expected rather than coincidental.
reasoning: STAT1, IRF1, IRF2, TBX21 and IKZF1 each have direct disease-specific evidence in both lung cancer and melanoma, and several are addressed together in the same publications on radiotherapy-induced immune modulation, GBP2-STAT1 signalling and anti-PD-L1 sensitisation; AIRE's role is anchored by joint papers on immune-related adverse events under checkpoint inhibition, which is the accepted mechanistic bridge between the two cancers' shared immunotherapy biology. The module is nameable from the factors alone (IFN-gamma-STAT1-IRF1/2 antigen presentation plus TBX21/IKZF1 lymphocyte programme plus AIRE/FOXN1 tolerance), so this clears the bar for 'strong' even though the underlying comparisons come from a single cohort pair.
support: PMID 42020516 (IRF1-TRIM21 axis and anti-tumour immunity, lung cancer, also flagged as concerning both diseases); PMID 41286130 (GBP2 regulates lung cancer progression through STAT1, joint); PMID 41444224 (GBP2 condensates and STAT1-linked ferroptosis sensitise melanoma to anti-PD-L1, joint); PMID 40471501 (curcumin blocks IFN-gamma-induced PD-L1 via STAT1 phosphorylation in NSCLC, joint); PMID 41716028 (STAT1 drives melanoma progression via TUBB4A, joint); PMID 36370712 (IRF2 drives IFN-mediated CD8+ T-cell exhaustion, joint); PMID 40283008 (TBX21/GATA-3/FoxP3/RORgt immune modulation by stereotactic radiotherapy, explicitly both lung and melanoma); PMID 31160305 (blocking Aire-mediated central tolerance to enhance immunotherapy, joint); PMID 40930749 (innate/adaptive immune features of immune-related adverse events, joint); PMID 35053465 (biomarkers of immune-related adverse events under checkpoint inhibitors in metastatic melanoma); PMID 39154541 (IKZF1 methylation blood test for lung adenocarcinoma); PMID 42149258 (IKZF1-linked genomic mutation predicts anti-PD-1 survival in metastatic melanoma); PMID 40394429 (IKZF1 as a therapeutic target via Mendelian randomization, joint); PMID 39628682 (FOXN1 as prognostic marker in squamous NSCLC).
how_to_falsify: In matched lung-cancer and melanoma cohorts starting anti-PD-1 therapy, score tumours for an IFN-gamma/STAT1-IRF1-IRF2 antigen-presentation signature and for TBX21/IKZF1 lymphocyte infiltration; if responders in one disease show no correlated induction of this signature relative to non-responders while the other disease does, or if AIRE/FOXN1 expression fails to track incidence of immune-related adverse events across both cohorts, the shared-axis claim fails. A cleaner test: STAT1 or IRF1 knockdown in paired NSCLC and melanoma lines co-cultured with autologous CD8 T cells should abolish MHC-I upregulation and T-cell killing to a similar degree in both if the module is truly shared; disease-specific abolition would falsify it.
caveats: Lung and skin are embryologically and anatomically unrelated, so any shared axis has to be immune-system-based, not tissue-based; the 252 patient-group comparisons derive from only 1 independent cohort pair, so the breadth of comparisons does not amount to independent replication. PAX5, FOXD3, ZBTB4, CRX and PAX4 are concordant by the network's ranking but were left out of carrying_factors because they read as separate programmes (B-cell lineage commitment, neural-crest/melanocyte specification, photoreceptor and pancreatic-islet biology respectively) with weak, single-paper, or off-topic support rather than as part of the immune axis. None of the single-view exclusions (PITX1, MYCN, SOX4, etc.) belong to the interferon/lymphocyte module, which argues the axis is not an artifact of one patient subgroup.
